NO. 011 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Laridae · Gulls & Terns

Black-headed Gull

红嘴鸥 · hóng zuǐ ōu Chroicocephalus ridibundus
Winter visitor Abundant 37–43 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The red-billed, red-legged gull that winters in Zhuhai

Every November they arrive in flocks from the north and settle on the water off Lovers' Road. Red bill, red legs, white body, and in winter a faint dark smudge behind the eye. They are the most conspicuous birds of a Zhuhai winter, and the first gull many people ever look at properly.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • Bill & legsBill and legs both bright red (duller in winter) — the most direct feature of the species.
  • HeadIn summer the whole head is dark chocolate-brown (not black); in winter the head is white with a grey-black ear-spot behind the eye.
  • PlumageBack and wings pale grey with a bold white wedge along the leading edge (a white flash in flight) and black wingtips.
  • SizeMedium, larger than Saunders's Gull, with a longer finer bill and a buoyant flight.

Behaviour

Highly gregarious, gathering in winter in harbours and estuaries in flocks of tens to hundreds, often following fishing boats and tide lines. Eats small fish, shrimp, insects and food offered by people. Adaptable enough to use city waterways, and quick in the air, turning sharply and plunging into the water.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • along Lovers' Road
  • Yeli Island shore
  • Xianglu Bay
  • Jinwan coast
Field note
Please don't feed them bread or processed food: it causes malnutrition and dependency. Keep your distance and let them forage.
